concept.name: Strategic asset allocation
concept.definition: The long-term target allocation across asset classes that an investor commits to based on goals, time horizon, and risk tolerance, typically reviewed over years or decades and maintained through periodic rebalancing.
concept.intuition: It is the 'default setting' of the portfolio - the mix you plan to hold through market cycles rather than the mix you happen to hold today.
concept.mechanics: Target weights are derived from long-term capital market expectations and the investor's circumstances; actual weights are periodically rebalanced back to the policy targets, and the policy itself is revisited only when goals, horizon, or risk tolerance change materially.
concept.failure_modes: A strategic mix built on stale long-run return, volatility, or correlation assumptions can silently deliver a very different risk profile than intended, and rigid adherence can be costly if the investor's circumstances change mid-horizon.
concept.misconceptions: Strategic allocation is not 'buy and forget': it requires rebalancing to stay at target weights and periodic re-derivation when the investor's situation changes.
concept.example: A pension plan sets a policy mix of 60% equities and 40% fixed income, rebalancing annually; this 60/40 target itself - not any short-term deviation from it - is the strategic asset allocation.
